response.sql: SELECT r.raceId, r.name, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(NULLIF(res.laps, ''), '\N') AS REAL)) AS avgLaps FROM races r LEFT JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId AND res.positionOrder >= 12 GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name ORDER BY avgLaps IS NULL, avgLaps DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Missing `laps` values are stored as NULL, an empty string, or the literal '\N'; these are excluded before averaging. The schema and documentation do not specify the encoding, so this is inferred.
All races are listed, including races with no results at positionOrder >= 12, which get a NULL average and sort last. This follows the request's note that races lacking an average go last.
Each race's `name` is unique within its `raceId`, so grouping by both does not split any race.

alternatives.interpretation: Include only races that have at least one result with positionOrder >= 12, dropping races with no qualifying results entirely rather than listing them with a NULL average.
